rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should give generously while able, before death prevents spending and other righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: ما داموا مقتدرين قبل الفوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person sensing death may plead for delay and healing to make up good deeds; the appeal expresses hope that God may grant the request.
rows.anchor: حين يحس المرء بحالة تؤذن بقرب الموت ويغلب على قواه فيسأل الله أن يؤخر موته ويشفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لولا is an urgent exhortation here; elsewhere it can introduce an appeal, rebuke, regret, or figurative wish.
rows.anchor: و { لولا } حرف تحضيض ، والتحضيض الطلب الحثيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although lولا normally takes an imperfect verb, the past form intensifies the plea as if its fulfillment were certain; the following results support this reading.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاء ماضيا هنا لتأكيد إيقاعه في دعاء الداعي حتى كأنه قد تحقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea asks God urgently to postpone death briefly so the believer can make up neglected charity and good works.
rows.anchor: أن يحقق تأخير موته إلى أجل يستدرك فيه ما اشتغل عنه من إنفاق وعمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the requested term near reflects the common belief that a small request is likelier to be granted; the Qur'an reports people's customary speech.
rows.anchor: الأمر اليسير أرجى لأن يستجيبه المسؤول فيغلب ذلك على شعورهم حين يسألون الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The cited hadith warns worshippers to ask firmly for forgiveness rather than making it conditional on God's will.
rows.anchor: لا يقولن أحدكم : اللهم اغفر لي إن شئت وليعزم المسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjunctive فأصدق follows the request with an obligatorily omitted أن.
rows.anchor: وانتصب فعل { فأصدق } على إضمار ( أن ) المصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read وأكن jussive as a direct response to the request; the waw joins clauses, not individual verbs, so no causal fāʾ appears.
rows.anchor: فأما الجمهور فقرأوه مجزوما بسكون آخره على اعتباره جوابا للطلب مباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive also implies a condition: if God grants the short delay, the speaker will become righteous, combining consequence with conditionality.
rows.anchor: فتقديره : إن تؤخرني إلى أجل قريب أكن من الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خبير is preferred to عليم because it conveys knowledge of hidden matters, including inward resolve and intention as well as outward deeds.
rows.anchor: وإيثار وصف { خبير } دون : عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death interrupting a good deed whose legally appointed time remains open does not deprive a believer of its reward, including a regular devotional practice or intended Hajj.
rows.anchor: أن حيلولة الموت دون إتمامه لا يرزىء المؤمن ثوابه لأن المؤمن إذا اعتاد حزبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer who regularly performs a devotional portion or resolves to do good but is prevented receives its reward.
rows.anchor: إذا اعتاد حزبا أو عزم على عمل صالح ثم عرض له ما منعه منه أن الله يعطيه أجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites an authentic hadith that a good deed intended but left undone is recorded as one complete good deed.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل : أن من هم بحسنة فلم يعملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read تعملون with second-person ت, addressing the listeners.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { بما تعملون } بالمثناة الفوقية

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: This reader uses third-person ي; its pronoun refers to the generic singular نفسا, which has plural sense in the negation.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو بكر عن عاصم بالمثناة التحتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed subject of يجمعكم is God, named in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: والضمير المستتر في { يجمعكم } عائد إلى اسم الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يجمعكم means gathering all people and nations; the Qur'an elsewhere calls it the gathering of you and the first generations.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { يجمعكم } يجمع المخاطبين والأمم من الناس كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the gathering may mean resurrecting the bones, further confirming the resurrection the unbelievers denied.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الجمع الذي في قوله تعالى : { أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ليوم الجمع may express purpose: God gathers people for the appointed day on which everyone is gathered for judgment; the two uses of gathering form wordplay, not circular reasoning.
rows.anchor: واللام في { ليوم الجمع } يجوز أن يكون للتعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical possibility makes the lām mean في, as in expressions for an event occurring at or in its time.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون اللام بمعنى ( في ) على نحو ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the lām of timing, meaning عند: people are gathered at the appointed time without delay, rebutting their denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: والأحسن عندي أن يكون اللام للتوقيت ، وهي التي بمعنى ( عند )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم الجمع is the Day of Resurrection and a title for it; a hadith says God gathers the first and last generations.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث ( يجمع الله الأولين والآخرين ) الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence interrupts the link between the prior warning that deeds will be disclosed and the promise to believers, magnifying the Day and warning idolaters of loss.
rows.anchor: اعتراض بين جملة { ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم } ( التغابن : 7 ) بمتعلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative instead of a pronoun draws attention to this Day and, as a distant demonstrative, suggests its elevated rank.
rows.anchor: والإتيان باسم الإشارة في مقام الضمير لقصد الاهتمام بهذا اليوم بتمييزه أكمل تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghabun is the reciprocal verbal noun of غابن; the reciprocal form ordinarily describes an act shared by two or more parties.
rows.anchor: والتغابن } : مصدر غابنه من باب المفاعلة الدالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sale's غبن is selling below fair value, making the seller the loser; the word extends metaphorically to loss generally, as al-Aʿsha's verse shows.
rows.anchor: والغبن أن يعطى البائع ثمنا لمبيعه دون حق قيمته التي يعوض بها مثله

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: The cited line uses غبن الخاسر to attest the word's sense of loss.
rows.anchor: لا يقبل الرشوة في حكمه ولا يبالي غبن الخاسر

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والحسن
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes take the reciprocal literally: the people of Paradise have gained over the people of Hell, each receiving the other's contrasting outcome.
rows.anchor: ففسروها بأن أهل الجنة غبنوا أهل النار إذ أهل الجنة أخذوا الجنة وأهل جهنم أخذوا جهنم قاله مجاهد وقتادة والحسن

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi and others explain the reported view as an analogy between the two groups and traders, one receiving fair value and the other a defrauded price.
rows.anchor: فحمل القرطبي وغيره كلام هؤلاء الأيمة على أن التغابن تمثيل لحال الفريقين بحال متبايعين

rows.speaker: الراغب وابن عطية
rows.claim: A minority understand the reciprocal form as intensity or abundance, a metaphor for the great loss of the disbelievers rather than mutual exchange.
rows.anchor: وصرح ابن عطية صيغة التفاعل على معنى الكثرة وشدة الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the reciprocal form figuratively for abundant loss; the disbelievers suffer this loss, with God as the one who causes it.
rows.anchor: فصيغة التفاعل مستعملة مجازا في كثرة حصول الغبن تشبيها للكثرة بفعل من يحصل من متعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse threatens idolaters with their severe loss on the Day of Gathering, in the context of the call to believe in God, His Messenger, and the revealed Light.
rows.anchor: والكلام تهديد للمشركين بسوء حالتهم في يوم الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the Day of Loss makes sense because believers gain greatly on that Day; he compares the contrast with failed trade and the Prophet's definition of the bankrupt person.
rows.anchor: ولولا قصد ذلك لما اقتصر على أن ذلك يوم تغابن فإن فيه ربحا عظيما للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The cited hadith identifies the true bankrupt person as one who is bankrupt on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إنما المفلس الذي يفلس يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defining both parts of the sentence restricts the kind of Day of Loss to this Day alone; worldly market losses count as negligible by comparison.
rows.anchor: وأفاد تعريف جزأي جملة { ذلك يوم التغابن } قصر المسند على المسند إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in التغابن marks the genus of loss; other verses contrast ultimate loss with commerce that never fails.
rows.anchor: وأما لام التعريف في قوله : { التغابن } فهي لام الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls this the decisive interpretation and criticizes commentators for passing over the verse's rhetorical force.
rows.anchor: هذا هو المتعين في تفسير هذه الآية وأكثر المفسرين مر بها مرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to believers coordinates with the command to believe in 64:8 and spells out what God's comprehensive knowledge means.
rows.anchor: معطوفة على جملة { فآمنوا بالله ورسوله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional promise includes any polytheist who believes after this admonition; السيئات means disbelief and earlier corrupt deeds.
rows.anchor: أي من يؤمن من المشركين بعد هذه الموعظة نكفر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expiating sins means pardoning liability for them; the intensive form derives metaphorically from covering something in order to remove it, as with forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وتكفير السيئات : العفو عن المؤاخذة بها وهو مصدر كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صالحا describes an omitted verbal noun, with the implied wording عملا صالحا.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { صالحا } على الصفة لمصدر وهو مفعول مطلق محذوف

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers use first-person plural نكفر and ندخله, shifting from third person to a welcoming first-person promise.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر { نكفر } و { ندخله } بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: باقي القراء
rows.claim: The other readers keep the third-person forms, following the apparent discourse and the preceding mention of God.
rows.anchor: وقرأهما الباقون بياء الغيبة على مقتضى الظاهر لأن ضمير الجلالة يؤذن بعناية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك الفوز العظيم is a concluding summary of the promise.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ذلك الفوز العظيم } تذييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who persisted in disbelief and denial did not answer the call and are thereby established as people of the Fire; the nominal sentence conveys their settled state.
rows.anchor: كفروا وكذبوا من قبل واستمروا على كفرهم وتكذيبهم فلم يستجيبوا لهذه الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative singles out the condemned group and signals that their lasting punishment follows from disbelief and denial of God's signs.
rows.anchor: وجيء لهم باسم الإشارة لتمييزهم تمييزا لا يلتبس معه غيرهم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بئس المصير is a parenthetic summary that heightens the threat.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وبئس المصير } اعتراض تذييلي لزيادة تهويل الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage shifts to console Muslims for persecution in Mecca, including bodily and financial harm and discord within families; God knows what they endure.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لم يكفوا عن أذى المسلمين وإصابتهم في أبدانهم وأموالهم والفتنة بينهم وبين أزواجهم وأبنائهم

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: A reported occasion of revelation says unbelievers argued that if the Muslims' religion were true, God would have protected them from calamities.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي ( قيل سبب نزولها أن الكفار قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here spending means providing the necessities of life, including food and clothing.
rows.anchor: والإنفاق : كفاية مؤونة الحياة من طعام ولباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first من is source or origin: spending issues from one's means; unlike the partitive من in 8:3 and later in this verse, expenditure is not a portion of one's capacity.
rows.anchor: و { من } هنا ابتدائية لأن الإنفاق يصدر عن السعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the من in this verse, the من in 8:3 is partitive because spending is a portion of one's provision; here the second من is also partitive.
rows.anchor: فلذلك تكون ( من ) من قوله : { فلينفق مما آتاه الله } تبعيضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A restricted provision is limited means; whoever is financially constrained should spend within what they can afford, observing priorities and levels of duty.
rows.anchor: أي من كان في ضيق من المال فلينفق بما يسمح به رزقه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: He cites the Prophet's instruction to Hind, Abu Sufyan's wife, to take from her husband's property what suffices for her and her child according to recognized custom.
rows.anchor: قال النبي لهند بنت عتبة زوج أبي سفيان : خذي من ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognized custom is ordinary social practice unless Islamic law overrides it.
rows.anchor: والمعروف : هو ما تعارفه الناس في معتاد تصرفاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision includes useful necessities such as food, clothing, goods, and housing, whether supplied as objects or money; it often means food specifically.
rows.anchor: والرزق : اسم لما ينتفع به الإنسان في حاجاته من طعام ولباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree support has no fixed amount because circumstances, times, and places differ; they dispute how much an affluent provider owes beyond sufficiency.
rows.anchor: ولم يختلف العلماء في أن النفقات لا تتحدد بمقادير معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the disagreement over extra provision as a difference in people's conditions and customs, requiring attention to the dependent's circumstances and accustomed standard.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من اعتبار حال المنفق عليه ومعتاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction that God burdens no soul beyond what He gives explains the order to spend according to one's means and had already been established in 2:286.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها } تعليل لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This principle reassures the recipient not to demand more than the provider can afford; an insolvent provider who can feed and clothe dependents modestly without harm is not separated from them.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منه إقناع المنفق عليه بأن لا يطلب من المنفق أكثر من مقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God has given includes earning ability, so a capable provider can be compelled to work to support dependents or supplement inadequate means.
rows.anchor: يشمل المقدرة على الاكتساب فإذا كان من يجب عليه الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person cannot earn and has nothing to spend, support for that person and dependents falls to the Muslims' public treasury according to its obligations.
rows.anchor: وأما من لا قدرة له على الاكتساب وليس له ما ينفق منه فنفقته أو نفقة من يجب عليه إنفاقه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar asks whether he should abandon a herdsman whose small flock has perished when the herdsman brings proof and appeals to the commander; Malik reports it in the Muwatta.
rows.anchor: وقد قال عمر بن الخطاب : ( وأن رب الصريمة ورب الغنيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists disagree whether a wife may seek separation when her husband cannot provide: Malik allows it after a waiting period, estimated here at two months; Abu Hanifa does not, with support instead from the treasury.
rows.anchor: فمن الفقهاء من رأى ذلك موجبا بينهما بعد أجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the public treasury functions, it must support indigent spouses; if support cannot be obtained there, the judge should separate them rather than leave the wife in need.
rows.anchor: إن كان بيت المال قائما فإن من واجبه نفقة الزوجين المعسرين وإن لم يتوصل إلى الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of ease completes the preceding conclusion and encourages hope for dependents facing hardship.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام خبر مستعمل في بعث الترجي وطرح اليأس عن المعسر من ذوي العيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement means that God sometimes brings ease after hardship, so a distressed person may hope for relief; it does not promise every distressed person an end to hardship.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : عسى أن يجعل الله بعد عسركم يسرا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects forced readings that make this a universal promise to the Muslims of that time or to all compliant spenders, since experience can contradict them.
rows.anchor: فلا فائدة في التكلف بأن هذا وعد من الله للمسلمين الموحدين يومئذ بأن الله سيبدل عسرهم باليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite forms عسر and يسرا avoid suggesting the totality that definite forms could imply; he compares the wording in 94:5.
rows.anchor: ومن بلاغة القرآن الإتيان ب ( عسر ويسرا ) نكرتين غير معرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legal rulings of divorce are followed by encouragement to obey through promises of escape, ease, forgiveness, and reward.
rows.anchor: رغب في الامتثال لها بقوله : { ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings about violating God's limits and the final warning about peoples who ignored God and His messengers guard against treating the legal duties lightly.
rows.anchor: وحذر الله الناس في خلال ذلك من مخالفتها بقوله : { وتلك حدود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported interpretation sees the threatened mark on the nose as a humiliation on Judgment Day, because the man displayed arrogance and pride through his nose.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذا وعيد بتشويه أنفه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in بلوناهم refers to the deniers previously mentioned; the orchard parable begins a new section prompted by the preceding account of wealth and children.
rows.anchor: ضمير الغائيبن في قوله : { بلوناهم } يعود إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable warns that pride in ample provision has long led people to scorn truth and neglect gratitude; similar examples appear in the Cave and the story of Qarun.
rows.anchor: فضرب الله للمشركين مثلا بحال أصحاب هذه الجنة لعلهم يستفيقون من غفلتهم وغرورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their trial was through blessings: Mecca enjoyed security, abundant provision, and easy trade across distant lands, yet its people rejected the messenger and failed to reflect on their gifts.
rows.anchor: فالبلوى المذكورة هنا بلوى بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans resemble the orchard owners in turning from seeking God's pleasure and thanking Him for His gifts.
rows.anchor: ووجه المشابهة بين حالهم وحال أصحاب الجنة المذكورة هنا هو الإعراض عن طلب مرضاة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable implicitly threatens a reversal from prosperity to distress; though the immediate cause differs, the same kind of punishment later struck the Meccans with seven famine years after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقد حصل ذلك بعد سنين إذ أخذهم الله بسبع سنين بعد هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orchard story was associated with Darwan near Sanaa in Yemen; some say Darwan was the garden's name.
rows.anchor: كانت ببلد يقال له : ضروان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the large garden belonged to a righteous, believing man from the People of the Book; the source does not identify him as Jewish or Christian.
rows.anchor: غرسها رجل من أهل الصلاح والإيمان من أهل الكتاب قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some say its owner was Jewish, reasoning that Yemen became Jewish in Bilqis's era or later and that Torah law required a tithe from fruit.
rows.anchor: فقيل : كان يهوديا

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Others place the owners shortly after Jesus, before Christianity spread in Yemen, which they date to the Abyssinian conquest near the Year of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : كان أصحاب هذه الجنة بعد عيسى بقليل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the owners were Abyssinians: their father shared the harvest with the poor, who supported orphans and widows, but his three wealthy sons became stingy and plotted to exclude them.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : كانوا من الحبشة كانت لأبيهم جنة وجعل في ثمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They planned to harvest before dawn before the poor arrived; their oath may have bound a hesitant brother, explaining why the middle brother later asks whether they would heed his warning.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن بعضهم كان مترددا في موافقتهم على ما عزموا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hesitant brother is said to have urged them to fear God, abandon their evil plan, and remember God's punishment; the others overruled him and secured the group's participation by oath.
rows.anchor: قيل كان يقول لهم : اتقوا الله واعدلوا عن خبث نيتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طاف literally means walking around something; here it portrays the calamity as affecting the entire garden, as a specter does in 7:201.
rows.anchor: الطواف : المشي حول شيء من كل جوانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition على with طاف gives the sense of taking control or descending upon the garden.
rows.anchor: وعدي ( طاف ) بحرف ( على ) لتضمينه معنى : تسلط أو نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calamity's kind is left unnamed because its effect matters, not its type; attributing the action to a طائف functions like a passive construction.
rows.anchor: ولم يعين جنس الطائف لظهور أنه من جنس ما يصيب الجنات من الهلاك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says a طائف only comes at night, associating the word with a dream specter; Ibn Ashur questions the proposed derivation from part of the night.
rows.anchor: وعن الفراء : أن الطائف لا يكون إلا بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase وهم نائمون either specifies when the calamity struck or, on al-Farra's reading, reinforces the nighttime sense and depicts the scene.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { وهم نائمون } تقييد لوقت الطائف على التفسير الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite طائف magnifies the event; the next verse identifies it as a ruinous calamity, with a report that a fiery blast burned the garden.
rows.anchor: وتنوين { طائف } للتعظيم ، أي أمر عظيم وقد بينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported explanation says a blast of fire struck and burned the garden.
rows.anchor: قيل : أصابها عنق من نار فاحترقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ربك means sent from God: the destruction was punishment for failing to give thanks.
rows.anchor: ف { من } للابتداء يعني : أنه عذاب أرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment came before they actually withheld charity because their settled resolve and oath made them culpable as if they had already withheld it.
rows.anchor: وعجل العقاب لهم قبل التلبس بمنع الصدقة لأن عزمهم على المنع وتقاسمهم عليه حقق أنهم مانعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage admonishes people who do not share their wealth; the garden's worldly punishment does not prove its owners withheld obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: ويؤخذ من الآية موعظة للذين لا يواسون بأموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes الصريم as night, also a name for day because each cuts off the other; pairing it with أصبح creates antithesis.
rows.anchor: والصريم قيل : هو الليل

rows.speaker: جذيمة أو خزيمة
rows.claim: Another reported dialectal meaning of الصريم is black ash.
rows.anchor: وقيل الصريم : الرماد الأسود بلغة جذيمة أو خزيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reported meaning of الصريم is a known barren sand tract in Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقيل الصريم : اسم رملة معروفة باليمن لا تنبت شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He favors the word's many meanings because all of them can suit the verse; يصرمنها and الصريم also form paronomasia.
rows.anchor: وإيثار كلمة الصريم هنا لكثرة معانيها وصلاحية جميع تلك المعاني لأن تراد في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in فتنادوا derives the call from their oath: at morning they summon one another to carry out the plan.
rows.anchor: وفاء { فتنادوا } للتفريع على { أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين ، }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling one another suggests urging each other to go early; غدو means leaving at the start of the day.
rows.anchor: والتنادي : أي ينادي بعضهم بعضا وهو مشعر بالتحريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن كنتم صارمين is not a real condition but an impatient prod, as if delay meant they would miss that day's harvest; Ibn Umar used similar phrasing to urge al-Hajjaj at Arafat.
rows.anchor: وليس قوله : { إن كنتم صارمين } بشرط تعليق ولكنه مستعمل في الاستبطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umar told al-Hajjaj to proceed from Arafat at the proper time, saying that if he wanted the Sunna he should move on.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عبد الله بن عمر للحجاج عند زوال عرفة يحرضه على التهجير بالرواح إلى الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على حرثكم means reaching and settling at the orchard; alternatively غدا includes the sense of approaching, as in a line cited by al-Tibi about a whip and a serving bowl.
rows.anchor: و { على } من قوله : { على حرثكم } مستعملة في تمكن الوصول إليه

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi cites the expression about a whip going out to fools and a bowl to the forbearing as a parallel construction.
rows.anchor: قال الطيبي : ( ومثله قيل في حق المطلب تغدو درته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harth literally means working soil to plant seeds or trees and remove weeds; here it means the garden maintained through cultivation.
rows.anchor: والحرث : شق الأرض بحديدة ونحوها ليوضع فيها الزريعة أو الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: التخافت is the reciprocal form of خفت, speaking quietly.
rows.anchor: والتخافت : تفاعل من خفت إذا أسر الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase forbidding any poor person to enter explains the whispering, since تخافت implies speech without stating its words.
rows.anchor: وأن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين } تفسير لفعل { يتخافتون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic ن in the prohibition reinforces their oath; grammatically the poor person is barred from entering, but the intended command is that no brother let one in.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد فعل النهي بنون التوكيد لزيادة تحقيق ما تقاسموا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وغدوا على حرد قادرين is a circumstantial clause with an implicit قد, describing their state as they set out.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وغدوا على حرد قادرين } في موضع الحال بتقدير ( قد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating غدوا in the circumstantial clause makes their ill-fated early departure striking; Ibn al-Qays's verse similarly turns back to the night already described.
rows.anchor: وذكر فعل { غدوا } في جملة الحال لقصد التعجيب

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: The quoted verse about spending the night awake illustrates the rhetorical return to an already-mentioned night.
rows.anchor: وبات وباتت له ليلة كليلة ذي العائر الأرمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حرد can mean prevention, forceful purpose or speed, or anger.
rows.anchor: والحرد : يطلق على المنع وعلى القصد القوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word's selection has a rhetorical subtlety because its different meanings attach aptly either to قادرين or to غدوا.
rows.anchor: وفي إيثار كلمة { حرد } في الآية نكتة من نكت الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If حرد modifies قادرين, the fronted phrase restricts them to being able to withhold good or fruit, not help anyone; calling this ability is ironic.
rows.anchor: فإذا علق ب { قادرين ، } فتقديم المتعلق يفيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If حرد means speed or resolve, it modifies غدوا and describes their energetic haste; قادرين then conveys their mistaken confidence that they could accomplish their aim.
rows.anchor: وإذا حمل الحرد على معنى السرعة والقصد كان { على حرد } متعلقا ب { غدوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading foreshadows their failure, confirmed by their response on seeing the ruined garden and by the preceding calamity.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام تعريض بأنهم خابوا ، دل عليه قوله بعده { فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If حرد means anger, the phrase means they could do nothing but rage at the poor, having failed to gather the fruit they sought; the fronting restricts their capacity to anger.
rows.anchor: وإذا أريد بالحرد الغضب والحنق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says حرد is the name of their village or orchard; Ibn Ashur suspects this is a contrived explanation drawn from the verbs اغدوا and غدوا.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي : أن { حرد } اسم قريتهم ، أي جنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners wake from heedlessness and blame themselves for pride and failure to thank God; this fulfills the lesson that trials may turn people back.
rows.anchor: أي استفاقوا من غفلتهم ورجعوا على أنفسهم باللائمة على بطرهم وإهمال شكر النعمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء الله الإسكندري
rows.claim: Ibn Ata Allah's maxim says that ingratitude exposes blessings to loss, while gratitude binds them fast.
rows.anchor: من لم يشكر النعم فقد تعرض لزوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لما makes the answer follow its condition immediately and instinctively; the story urges idolaters to repent as quickly as the owners regretted and sought a better replacement.
rows.anchor: وأفادت ( لما ) اقتران جوابها بشرطها بالفور والبداهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural attribution indicates that all the owners agreed on the reason for what struck them.
rows.anchor: وإسناد هذه المقالة إلى ضمير { أصحاب الجنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا لضالون means they had strayed from gratitude; calling that misguidance metaphorically signals their recognition that the disaster was punishment for ingratitude.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { إنا لضالون } أنهم علموا أنهم كانوا في ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording conveys grief and regret because they had only just recognized their earlier heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وأكدوا الكلام لتنزيل أنفسهم منزلة من يشك في أنهم ضالون طريق الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل shifts to the more serious point: they had planned to deprive the poor of surplus, but in fact they themselves lost all the fruit.
rows.anchor: و { بل نحن محرومون } إضراب للانتقال إلى ما هو أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the explicit pronoun نحن, where the passive's subject could remain implicit, signals an additional restriction: they are the ones truly deprived.
rows.anchor: بأن أتي به ضميرا بارزا مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن يكون ضميرا مستترا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they may literally have thought they had lost the road to the garden; بل then corrects them: this is their garden, destroyed and stripped of its produce.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الضلال حقيقيا ، أي ضلال طريق الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوسطهم means their best and most virtuous brother; وسط can describe excellence, as in the community and prayer verses.
rows.anchor: و { أوسطهم } أفضلهم وأقربهم إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His saying lacks a conjunction because it answers their claim that they were deprived and reproaches them for disregarding his sound advice.
rows.anchor: وحكي هذا القول بدون عاطف لأنه قول في مجرى المحاورة جوابا عن قولهم { بل نحن محرومون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is confirmatory, and لولا is an exhortation; تسبحون means declaring God free of disobedience by giving the poor their share.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري و { لولا } حرف تحضيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply acknowledges that he had warned them and they disobeyed; their glorification recognizes that they violated God's command to give the poor their due.
rows.anchor: وكان جوابهم يتضمن إقرارا بأنه وعظهم فعصوه ودلوا على ذلك بالتسبيح حين ندمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance begins with acknowledging harm to the poor and restoring what can be restored; glorifying God precedes asking forgiveness, as in 110:3.
rows.anchor: فإن من أصول التوبة تدارك ما يمكن تداركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا كنا ظالمين confesses guilt; إن emphasizes the admission and explains the preceding glorification, while the omitted object covers harm to themselves and to the poor.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { ظالمين } ليعم ظلمهم أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uncoordinated answer follows conversational narration, as in the cited exchange in the second chapter.
rows.anchor: وجرت حكاية جوابهم على طريقة المحاورة فلم تعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mutual blame compresses each brother's role: inventing the scheme, conspiring, accepting it, and carrying out the plan; the wording pictures attack and reproach.
rows.anchor: كل يلوم غيره بما كان قد تلبس به في هذا الشأن من ابتكار فكرة منع المساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their collective wail and confession may explain how they blamed each other, using indirect rebuke and remorse; the sentence is then explanatory and uncoordinated.
rows.anchor: فجملة { قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا طاغين } إلى آخرها يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each answers the others in dialogue, admitting guilt and hoping God will forgive them and replace the garden with a better one in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جواب بعضهم بعضا عن لومه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word جمع signals greed and فأوعى suggests long hopes; he reads the latter as hoarding and holding onto accumulated vices.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { جمع } إشارة إلى الحرص

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets جمع فأوعى as collecting evil things and storing them, persisting in those bad traits.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة { جمع فأوعى } كان جموعا للخبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 19–21 interrupt the discussion between the one who hoards and the exception for worshippers; they summarize the human trait that drives greed and retention.
rows.anchor: معترضة بين { من أدبر وتولى وجمع فأوعى } ( المعارج : 17 18 ) وبين الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a rebuke, not an excuse or justification for hoarding; fear of losing what benefits them explains the trait but does not absolve it.
rows.anchor: وهذا تذييل لوم وليس في مساقه عذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic إن draws attention to the startling human trait and warns against it.
rows.anchor: وموقع حرف التوكيد ما تتضمنه الجملة من التعجيب من هذه الخصلة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main point is withholding when touched by good; being distressed when touched by harm prepares and completes the paired description.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من التذييل هو قوله : { وإذا مسه الخير منوعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإنسان denotes humanity as a species, not one individual, as in verses about human arrogance and haste.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالإنسان : جنس الإنسان لا فرد معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هلوع is an intensive adjective describing a strong tendency to panic and withhold.
rows.anchor: وهلوع : فعول مثال مبالغة للاتصاف بالهلع

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى (ثعلب)
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf recounts Thalab's definition to Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir: the verse itself defines the person who intensely despairs at harm and keeps good from others.
rows.anchor: وعن أحمد بن يحيى ( هو ثعلب ) قال لي محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says Thalab's definition is loose and imprecise: if the two following clauses define one compound trait, their distinct meanings would need to entail each other.
rows.anchor: فسارت كلمة ثعلب مسيرا أقنع كثيرا من اللغويين عن زيادة الضبط لمعنى الهلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many linguists equate halʿ with distress, but distress is an effect of halʿ rather than the trait itself; the distinction is tested by the cited verse of Amr ibn Ma'dikarib.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا من أيمة اللغة فسر الهلع بالجزع

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: His line distinguishes halʿ from jazaʿ by denying both separately; al-Marzūqī's attempt to read them as mild and severe grief does not resolve the difficulty.
rows.anchor: ما إن جزعت ولا هلعت ولا يرد بكاي زندا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defines halʿ as weak self-restraint when facing or anticipating what saddens or pleases a person.
rows.anchor: أن الهلع قلة إمساك النفس عند اعتراء ما يحزنها أو ما يسرها أو عند توقع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other lexical glosses include greed, irritation, miserliness, hunger, or cowardice; these are effects of the broader trait he defines.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر بعض أهل اللغة الهلع بالشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being created halūʿ means this tendency is latent in human nature and appears when people first perceive benefit or harm; it does not preclude contrary states or moral training.
rows.anchor: أن الهلع طبيعة كامنة فيه مع خلقه تظهر عند ابتداء شعوره بالنافع والمضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the trait follows the condemnation of hoarding, the wording implies people can restrain it by considering consequences and disciplining their weaknesses.
rows.anchor: فقد أشعر بأن الإنسان يستطيع أن يكف عن هلعه إذا تدبر في العواقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means human cognition tends toward halʿ; saying it is created in people highlights how strongly the tendency can dominate them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن من مقتضى تركيب الإدراك البشري أن يحدث فيه الهلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing defects to human creation assigns responsibility: people fail to train their good disposition, indulge their impulses, and neglect the advice of revelation and wise people.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود من ذلك : إلقاء تبعة ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing good to God recalls His gift of the faculty that seeks good and His guidance and awakening to truth, as 4:78–79 explains.
rows.anchor: وإذا أسند ما يأتيه الإنسان من الخير إلى الله تعالى فالمقصود : التنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Mu'tazilites went astray in this theological question.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المجال زلت أفهام المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When خلق الإنسان describes a nonmaterial trait, it can mean a human disposition quickly attaches to feelings and actions, warning against its harm, as in the description of haste.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن كلمة ( خلق الإنسان ) إذا تعلق بها ما ليس من المواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation wording can also soften blame by noting human weakness, or distinguish original good creation from later deterioration.
rows.anchor: وقد ترد للعذر والرفق نحو قوله : { يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلق from a trait can be metaphorical for persistent association; Urwa ibn Udhayna's poem argues that love remains because both lovers were created disposed to it.
rows.anchor: ففعل الخلق من كذا مستعار لكثرة الملابسة . قال عروة بن أذينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading of Hamza, Asim, and Abu Ja'far, قل إني لا أملك repeats قل إنما أدعو ربي from the previous verse.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { قل إني لا أملك } الخ ، تكريرا لجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضر alludes to their taunts demanding that the threatened victory over them be hastened; ولا رشدا completes the statement.
rows.anchor: والضر : إشارة إلى ما يتوركون به من طلب إنجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing omits corresponding terms: harm implies benefit, and right guidance implies misguidance.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام احتباك لأن الضر يقابله النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd is a verbal noun with fatḥa; الرشد with ḍamma is the noun for knowing what is correct, as in 72:2.
rows.anchor: والرشد بفتحتين : مصدر رشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا أملك لكم means having no power on their behalf to bring harm or benefit; he points to similar expressions in al-Mumtahana and al-A'raf.
rows.anchor: وتركيب { لا أملك لكم } معناه لا أقدر قدرة لأجلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sentences about having no protector and no refuge interrupt the surrounding exception; they answer the demand that the Prophet stop condemning their beliefs and idols.
rows.anchor: وجملتا قل إني لن يجيرني } إلى { ملتحدا } معترضتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملتحد is a place of turning aside for refuge, especially an asylum; the meaning is that the Prophet will find no place to protect him.
rows.anchor: والملتحد : اسم مكان الالتحاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من دونه describes a refuge outside God's dominion, which cannot exist; لن therefore emphatically denies finding one.
rows.anchor: أي ملتحدا كائنا من دون الله أي بعيدا عن الله غير داخل من ملكوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The من before دون is an extra preposition governing the adverb.
rows.anchor: و { من } في قوله : { من دونه } مزيدة جارة للظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for delivering God's message is disconnected from the denied harm and guidance, which concern coercive influence; it may also be construed as excepting refuge, understood as safety or asylum.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إلا بلاغا من الله ورسالاته } استثناء منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception confirms the point through wording that resembles its opposite.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستثناء من أسلوب تأكيد الشيء بما يشبه ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلاغ is a verbal noun used for the delivered message; من marks its source as God, and رسالاته refers to conveying the Qur'an in its revealed words.
rows.anchor: و { من } ابتدائية صفة ( بلاغ )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage threatens those who persist in disobeying God and His Messenger with Hell; من introduces the condition.
rows.anchor: أعقب ذلك بتهديدهم ووعيدهم بأنهم إن داموا على عصيان الله ورسوله سيلقون نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers mocked promises of victory and punishment and mistook respite for proof they would prevail, so the threat continues until they see what was promised.
rows.anchor: فهم مغرورون بالاستدراج والإمهال فلذلك عقب وعيدهم بالغاية المفادة من { حتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated البشر in this passage and لواحة للبشر is complete paronomasia.
rows.anchor: وبين لفظ البشر المذكور هنا ولفظ البشر المتقدم في قوله : { لواحة للبشر } التجنيس التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا is a rebuke and rejection, usually responding to a claim by the same or another speaker; the cited passages illustrate this function.
rows.anchor: { كلا } حرف ردع وإبطال . والغالب أن يقع بعد كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا may be moved ahead to reject the preceding claim about the parable, with the intervening material parenthetical and the oath beginning a new statement; this permits a pause after كلا.
rows.anchor: ويجوز تقديمه على الكلام إذا أريد التعجيل بالردع والتشويق إلى سماع ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, كلا rejects in advance the following claim that the passage is a warning to humanity, since people should heed it but most do not; this favors joining it in recitation.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون حرف إبطال مقدما على الكلام الذي بعده من قوله : { إنها لإحدى الكبر نذيرا للبشر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening waw may introduce an oath that concludes the preceding rejection of the claim about Hell's guards; إنها لحدى الكبر then explains the rejection, with its pronoun referring to Saqar.
rows.anchor: وهذا القسم يجوز أن يكون تذييلا لما قبله مؤكدا لما أفادته { كلا } من الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath begins the following statement, and إنها لحدى الكبر is its response; the pronoun again refers to Saqar, the greatest of terrors.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون القسم صدرا للكلام الذي بعده وجملة { إنها لإحدى الكبر } جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three oath clauses repeat emphasis, conventionally three times, and swear by a great created object and two great signs of God's power.
rows.anchor: وهذه ثلاثة أيمان لزيادة التأكيد فإن التأكيد اللفظي إذا أكد بالتكرار يكرر ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moon, departing night, and brightening dawn are apt oaths because their lights appear amid darkness, evoking guidance and misguidance and the Qur'an's light.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة القسم ب { القمر والليل إذ أدبر والصبح إذا أسفر } أن هذه الثلاثة تظهر بها أنوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night departs as dawn approaches, while dawn begins to show its light.
rows.anchor: وإدبار الليل : اقتراب تقضيه عند الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ and إذا are time adverbs functioning circumstantially for night and dawn; the ordered transition from darkness to light recalls Islam removing disbelief, as in 14:1.
rows.anchor: وكل من { إذ } و { إذا } واقعان اسمي زمان منتصبان على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is used like a proverb; إحدى means uniquely prominent among the greatest calamities, not merely one item in a group.
rows.anchor: وقد أجريت جملة { إنها لإحدى الكبر } مجرى المثل . ومعنى { إحدى } أنها المتوحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with one among the notable men and the proverb إحدى حظيات لقمان illustrates distinction and prominence.
rows.anchor: كما تقدم في قوله : { ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا }

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة وحفص ويعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: These readers have إذ أدبر, with إذ and a past-tense form: the oath is by the recurring moment when night has departed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة وحفص ويعقوب وخلف { إذ أدبر } بسكون ذال { إذ }

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم والكسائي وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers have إذا دبر, with a future-time adverb and a plain verb meaning departed, parallel to إذا أسفر; both readings are sound.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم والكسائي وأبو جعفر { إذا دبر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الكبر is an irregular broken plural of الكبرى; the form treats the word as the name of a great calamity rather than a feminine adjective, unlike عظمى.
rows.anchor: و { الكبر } : جمع الكبرى في نوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نذيرا is circumstantial from the pronoun in إنها: Saqar is among the greatest calamities while warning humanity, and that alone suffices as a warning.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { نذيرا } على الحال من ضمير { إنها }
